scope: P1 fixed Matrix identity gateway, fenced internal provider renewal, bounded transport and current HRIS admission

validation.incrementalChecks: Final successful selection re-ran the 148 API cases after the two test-only catalog corrections. The 77 data, fourteen domain and complete worker graph had passed with the same production source in the preceding selection and were Gradle up-to-date.

behaviors: Opaque gateway access-token lookup only identifies the company/account/device/native-parent head; every request reacquires current HRIS permission, policy, MFA, client build, native and device authority.
The fixed provider WHOAMI route uses only an internal bearer and holds no SQL transaction; response publication reacquires all current authority and fences captured versions/deadlines.
Concurrent internal JWT logins publish one encrypted credential generation. Losing candidates expire without logging out the winning E2EE device.
Public refresh during internal login prevents stale publication. Native refresh during a query invalidates only the old observation; a new query using the retained gateway can succeed.
Late permission removal, parent revocation, access expiry and scheduled company disablement suppress provider results. Failed login/query responses also give current HRIS denial precedence.
Publication, safe generation-only audit and outbox roll back on final admission failure. Interrupted login never publishes its candidate.
Real pinned Synapse identity acquisition/reuse runs with actual PostgreSQL. HTTP/security tests separately use a private owned HTTP provider and a fixture-controlled activation transition.

Public identity requires one Authorization header, rejects cookies/native tokens as substitute authority, duplicate headers, query parameters and known/chunked bodies, and returns only no-store protocol identity.
All private HTTP exchanges share 32 immediate permits, no waiting queue, fixed origins, no redirects, a five-second maximum and bounded 64 KiB response. Interruption releases a saturated permit.
Two legacy client-policy HTTP assertions now check the explicit nine-module catalog including COLLABORATION; the collaboration CI includes these tests.

correctedFailures.result: One of eighteen cases failed because the owned Synapse fixture had not been started before reading its repository. Added its explicit start; the provider and HTTP selection then passed.

Two old client-policy tests expected eight enabled modules after schema 105 added the ninth. Other 77 API cases, 77 data cases, fourteen domain cases and 110 worker cases passed; one existing retention case skipped.
Jackson 3 JsonNode.map applies to the node, not its array children. Switched the two assertions to iterator/asSequence before mapping strings.
correctedFailures.otherSuites: 148 API cases: 146 pass, two assertion failures; 77 collaboration data and fourteen domain cases pass; worker has 110 passes and the one existing opt-in retention skip.

limits: Only fixed identity GET and standard refresh POST are exposed. No Matrix sync, key API, room/content operation, public login/logout/admin/federation or browser-parent gateway is enabled.
The private fixture controls API activation; worker/Synapse provisioning is independently verified by existing worker integration tests.
Provider credentials rejected before stored expiry are surfaced as unavailability, without automatic device deletion or hidden provider retry.
No production schema/service configuration, phone installation or employee messaging occurred. Current schema is still 103; repository migration ceiling remains 109.
No new Matrix dependencies, native product UI, reusable Starter port, capacity or offline-chat acceptance is claimed.
